edition_notes: Rulebook in French (Règles du jeu), © 2018 SMILE LIFE, author and illustrator Alexandre Seba; 200-card deck.

items.rule: Shuffle all cards and deal 5 cards to each player; players keep their hands secret until the end of the game.
The remaining cards form a face-down draw pile.
The player with the most smiles in their starting hand begins.
On your turn, draw one card and then play one card of your choice from your hand, so you always keep 5 cards in hand.
Cards are always played face up: in front of yourself (to build your life and score smiles), in front of another player (to penalize them with a malus), or onto the discard pile.
Instead of drawing from the pile, you may take the last card of the discard pile, but you must play it immediately.
You may not take back a card you discarded yourself (voluntarily or because of a malus), unless another player has taken it and discarded it in the meantime.
Studies: you may accumulate up to 6 study cards (single or double; a double counts as two levels). You can no longer study while you have a job.
Jobs: you may only play a job if you have at least the number of study levels shown on it (top left, between the laurels). You can hold only one job at a time.
Salaries: you need a job to play salaries. Number of banknote bundles on the job (1-4) = highest salary level allowed; salaries of levels up to that can be played one at a time in any order.
Flirts: you can play flirts while not married, up to 5 flirts. At least one flirt is required before you can marry.
If you play a flirt in the same place as another player's top uncovered flirt, you immediately take that flirt and place it on top of yours (this can give you a 6th flirt if you already have 5).
A flirt at the hotel or camping lets you play one child (no more) while that flirt is uncovered by another flirt or a marriage.

Marriage can be played only after flirting at least once; you cannot have two marriages at the same time, and you cannot flirt while married. Children can be played one by one only once married (or via hotel/camping flirt).

Adultery can only be played when married and lets you keep flirting without limit alongside your marriage; flirts made during adultery are kept (smiles count) even if adultery stops. You can stop it by discarding it on your turn, before or after drawing, then playing.
Resignation: instead of drawing, discard your job and skip your turn; you can then study again or take a new job, resuming studies where you left off.

Voluntary divorce: instead of drawing, discard your marriage and skip your turn; you can then flirt again and possibly remarry. Under adultery, the adultery goes to the discard with the marriage on top; you keep your children and adultery flirts.
Animals are free and can be played directly; all acquisitions (animals, trips, houses) can be accumulated one by one.

Trips and houses must be paid with salaries in front of you (house needs a minimum down payment, halved if you are married). Paid salaries are turned face down as invested: they cannot be reused or taken back but keep their smiles. There is no change given on overpayment.

Légion d'honneur can be played directly unless you are or have been a bandit or have committed an attentat. Grand prix d'excellence can only be played by a writer, researcher or journalist and raises salary to level 4 for that job; only one per job; distinctions cannot be taken back.
Grand prof can only be played if you are already a teacher; the teacher card is then discarded.
Malus cards are played on another player on your turn; they score no smiles, and the victim suffers the effect then keeps the malus turned face down. Malus cards cannot be played on yourself.

Malus effects: accident/maladie make the victim skip a turn; burn out (workers only) skips a turn; divorce (married only) loses the marriage; impôt (workers only) discards last salary; licenciement (workers only) discards the job; redoublement (students only) discards last study card; prison (bandit only) skips 3 turns and discards the bandit; attentat removes all children of all players from the game.

Professional advantages and statuses: fonctionnaire (teachers, police, military) cannot be fired; intérimaire (gardener, waiter, barman, plumber, stripper) can resign without skipping a turn; other jobs have specific advantages listed on the card, such as bandit immune to firing and tax.

Special cards are played directly on your turn for their action and score no smiles; once used they are turned face down and cannot be retrieved. Examples: étoile filante (take any card from the discard and play it), piston (play any job then draw back to 5), arc-en-ciel (play up to 3 cards in a row then redraw to 5), troc (swap a random card with a player), tsunami (all hands are shuffled and redealt).

Other special cards: anniversaire (each player gives you one salary of their choice), chance (look at the next 3 cards of the pile and play one, discard the others), héritage (counts as 3 salaries for purchases), vengeance (pass one of your received malus to any other player), casino (bet face-down salaries; the second bettor wins all if the two salaries are identical, otherwise the first player wins all).
The game ends when the draw pile is empty.
When the game ends, every player discards the cards still in their hand.

Each player counts the smiles printed in the top left of the cards played face to them (including invested salaries turned face down, kept adultery flirts and used grand prix); malus and special cards give no smiles.
An unchallenged casino bet is recovered at the end of the game and counts as a salary, worth one smile.
The player with the most smiles wins.
To change game length, play with the whole draw pile or with only a portion of it.
